profiles.name: Peter John Gabriel McMullen
profiles.description: Peter John Gabriel McMullen was an Irish republican held in United States custody in connection with a British extradition request. After earlier immigration proceedings, he was arrested and held for extradition on December 24, 1986. His case was among the extradition fights that tested whether Irish republican offences would be treated as political offences by United States courts.

profiles.name: Duncan Murphy
profiles.description: World War II conscientious objector who served with an Allied ambulance unit through North Africa, Italy, France, and Germany; was with British troops liberating Bergen-Belsen. After the war spent 20 years in the Shiloh Community. Joined Brian Willson on day 15 of the Veterans Fast for Life (September 15, 1986). In 1987 joined Nuremberg Action — the 40-day fast and ongoing blockade at Concord Naval Weapons Station — present in the broader blockade work that culminated in Willson's September 1, 1987 injury. Continued protesting at the School of the Americas at Fort Benning, GA, through later years.

Download visually inspected; reject pending resolution of caption conflict.

profiles.name: Isaac Camacho Negrón
profiles.description: Isaac Camacho Negrón was a member of Los Macheteros (the Boricua Popular Army), the clandestine Puerto Rican independence organization. He was charged in connection with the group's September 1983 robbery of the Wells Fargo depot in West Hartford, Connecticut — about $7 million taken to fund the independence struggle. He was acquitted of the robbery itself but convicted of conspiracy in 1989; his sentence was commuted under a 2000 clemency grant.

profiles.name: Luz María Berríos Berríos
profiles.description:
Macheteros member arrested in the 1985 federal sweep connected to the Wells Fargo Hartford expropriation. She was held at FCI Lexington, including in the controversial high-security control unit for women. Documented in PFOC Breakthrough magazine. BOP #24582-004.

Luz Berríos Berríos was arrested in the August 30, 1985 Macheteros operation and was a plea defendant in the Wells Fargo prosecution. Remaining obligations were resolved by Clinton's August 1999 commutation.

Luz Maria Berrios-Berrios was charged as part of the federal crackdown on Los Macheteros, a clandestine pro-independence organization accused by U.S. authorities of financing its operations through armed actions. Prosecutors alleged she helped handle and conceal proceeds from the 1983 Wells Fargo depot robbery in Connecticut, including managing money movements and participating in politically framed distributions of cash and toys.

She pleaded guilty to a conspiracy count and received a five-year sentence. Her case illustrates how organizers and logistical supporters were prosecuted alongside alleged operational leaders in the broader Los Macheteros investigation.

profiles.name: Carlos Ayes Suárez
profiles.description: Carlos M. “Pío” Ayes Suárez was an anthropology and archaeology student from Vega Baja, Puerto Rico, and an activist in the Puerto Rican Independence Party. Federal agents arrested him on August 30, 1985, during the government’s roundup of people accused in the Wells Fargo robbery case. He was released on bail before January 1986 and tried with other defendants in Hartford, Connecticut. On April 10, 1989, the jury acquitted Ayes Suárez of every charge. He later worked as an archaeologist, anthropologist, author, and historian in Puerto Rico.

Macheteros member arrested in the August 1985 federal sweep connected to the 1983 Wells Fargo Hartford expropriation. He was held at FCI Sheridan. Documented in PFOC Breakthrough magazine. BOP #03173-069.

Orlando Claudio González was a Puerto Rican independence activist arrested on August 30, 1985 in the mass FBI raids in Puerto Rico that targeted Los Macheteros (the Ejército Popular Boricua) in connection with the 1983 $7.2 million Wells Fargo expropriation in West Hartford, Connecticut. Held in extended pre-trial preventive detention without bail and prosecuted in Hartford federal court, the defendants asserted that U.S. courts lacked jurisdiction over Puerto Rican patriots. His was one of the appeals that led the Second Circuit, in late 1986, to order bail reconsidered for the defendants still held under the Bail Reform Act.
